text_overlays.text: Managers who had the TOUGHEST El Clásico debuts!
José Mourinho had just won the Champions League with Inter Milan,
so Real Madrid brought him in during the summer of 2010 as the man who was finally going to stop Pep Guardiola's Barcelona.
And heading into the first ever El Clásico, Real Madrid were unbeaten in La Liga,
and Mourinho himself had never lost a match by five goals in his entire managerial career.
But that record was about to be destroyed in the most humiliating way possible.
Xavi chips the ball over Casillas just 10 minutes into the game to make it one-nil,
and then Pedro scores eight minutes later to make it two-nil before Mourinho's Real Madrid even had the chance to make it to the 20th minute.
Then in the second half, Messi threads a perfect ball to David Villa, who scores in the 55th minute
and then again just three minutes later to make it four-nil.
Jeffren Suárez then scores in stoppage time to make the score five-nil,
while Sergio Ramos picks up a red card in the final seconds after a frustrated foul on Messi,
and Mourinho is just sitting on the bench completely helpless as Camp Nou is absolutely crazy around him.
But somehow, there was still more.
Right after the fifth goal went in, Gerard Piqué walked over to the Barcelona fans, raised his hand, and held up all five fingers.
It's called La Manita, meaning the little hand, representing the five goals scored.
That single image of Piqué holding up those five fingers became one of the most iconic moments in El Clásico history,
and to this day, Real Madrid fans have never forgiven him for it.

ending.last_words: Real Madrid fans have never forgiven him for it.
